mainTopic: Rescuing תפילין found in a field on שבת: the end of the משנה, why one pair (רבי מאיר) or two pairs (רבן גמליאל), and two explanations of the dispute.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about someone who finds תפילין in a field on שבת. If staying is dangerous, he covers them and leaves. רבי שמעון allows a human chain of people, each carrying less than four אמות. The same applies to a baby born in the field. The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's idea that a chain can take a barrel past the תחום. The גמרא asks whether the one-pair limit goes against רבי מאיר. רבא answers that rescue follows normal weekday wearing: many garments, but only one pair of תפילין. The גמרא then explains רבן גמליאל's two pairs. שבת is not a time for תפילין, they must be worn in their proper place, and both the head and the arm have room for two. Finally, the גמרא gives two ways to explain the dispute: whether שבת is a time for תפילין, or whether מצוות צריכות כוונה.

steps.title: In danger, he covers the תפילין and leaves
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if staying in the field is dangerous, the finder covers the תפילין and goes on his way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in a time of danger, he covers them and goes on his way.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is continuing its discussion of someone who finds תפילין in a field on שבת. If it is dangerous to stay, he does not have to bring them in. He covers them to protect their dignity and leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal rule is to bring the תפילין in by wearing them one pair at a time. When there is danger, the person's safety comes first. Covering the תפילין is the minimum he does to protect their honor.

keyTerms.meaning: Danger: here, a risk to one's life from staying outside the town
He covers them, to protect the תפילין from disgrace
And he goes on his way

phrases.english: And in a time of danger —
phrases.notes: For example, when it is dangerous to stay outside the city.

phrases.english: he covers them and goes on his way.
phrases.notes: He covers the תפילין and leaves them there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier part of the משנה (not here) about bringing in תפילין found in a field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a dangerous situation, one covers the found תפילין and leaves them.
steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַסַּכָּנָה מְכַסָּן וְהוֹלֵךְ לוֹ

steps.title: רבי שמעון's human chain for the תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון allows passing the תפילין from person to person until they reach the outermost courtyard of the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: He gives them to his friend, and his friend gives them to his friend, until they reach the outer courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון offers another way to save the תפילין. People pass them along a chain until they reach the first courtyard of the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person carries the תפילין less than four אמות. Carrying less than four אמות in a רשות הרבים is only a rabbinic prohibition, not a Torah one. The חכמים relaxed it here out of respect for the תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: He gives them to his friend
The outermost courtyard: the first protected place at the edge of the city
Four cubits: the distance that counts as a Torah-level act of carrying in a public domain

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
He gives them to his friend,
phrases.notes: The friend stands less than four cubits away.

phrases.english: and his friend to his friend,
until it reaches the outer courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative method of rescuing the תפילין, beyond wearing them or covering them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תפילין may be passed from person to person, each moving them less than four אמות, until they reach the outer courtyard.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר נוֹתְנָן לַחֲבֵירוֹ

steps.title: The same chain method for a baby born in the field
steps.stepSummary: A baby born in the field may also be passed from person to person, even through a hundred people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly his son: he gives him to his friend, and his friend to his friend, even a hundred people.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same chain method to a newborn baby born in a field on שבת. The baby can be passed along, even if it takes a hundred people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby who cannot walk counts as a burden that may not be carried in a רשות הרבים. Because each person carries him less than four אמות, the passing is permitted. The words "even a hundred" show that there is no limit on the number of people in the chain.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly his son: a baby born in the field
Even a hundred people in the chain

phrases.english: And similarly his son —
phrases.notes: A baby born in the field on שבת.

phrases.english: he gives him to his friend,
and his friend to his friend,
even a hundred.
phrases.notes: Even if the chain needs a hundred people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי שמעון's chain method from תפילין to a newborn son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby born in a field may be passed along a human chain of any length.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן בְּנוֹ נוֹתְנוֹ לַחֲבֵירוֹ

steps.title: רבי יהודה lets a barrel go past the תחום
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that a barrel may be passed from person to person, even beyond the שבת boundary.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: A person may give a barrel to his friend, and his friend to his friend, even beyond the תחום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה stretches the chain idea further. Even an ordinary barrel can be passed along, and it can even travel past the תחום שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reasons that no single person carried the barrel four אמות, so no one broke a rule. This goes further than the earlier cases in two ways. A barrel is not a holy object, and the תחום limit is a separate issue from carrying four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrel
Beyond the תחום: past the 2,000-אמה limit one may go on שבת

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A person may give a barrel to his friend,
and his friend to his friend,
even beyond the Shabbat boundary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the chain method to ordinary objects and to travel beyond the תחום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a barrel may be passed along a chain even past the תחום.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר נוֹתֵן אָדָם חָבִית לַחֲבֵירוֹ

steps.title: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה: an object goes no farther than its owner
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה that a barrel cannot travel farther than its owner may walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: This barrel may not go farther than the feet of its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against רבי יהודה. An object is tied to its owner's תחום, so passing it along cannot take it past where the owner himself may go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say the תחום limit is not about who carries the object. It is about the object belonging to its owner, so it shares his range. The chain trick may solve the four-אמות problem, but it does not solve the תחום problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The feet of its owner: the object's range follows its owner's range

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with this principle: an object's תחום is the same as its owner's. A chain of carriers can avoid carrying four אמות, but it cannot take an object farther than its owner may walk.

phrases.english: They said to him:
This one may not go
phrases.notes: "This one" means the barrel.

phrases.english: farther than the feet of its owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects רבי יהודה's extension of the chain method beyond the תחום.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the part of רבי יהודה's ruling that lets the object go beyond the תחום.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה ignores that an object's תחום is tied to its owner, no matter who is carrying it.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לֹא תְּהַלֵּךְ זוֹ יוֹתֵר מֵרַגְלֵי בְעָלֶיהָ

steps.title: The גמרא reads the משנה: only one pair at a time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה's wording that the finder may bring in only one pair of תפילין at a time, not more.
steps.simpleTranslation: One pair, yes; more, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by looking closely at the earlier ruling in the משנה, that the finder brings the תפילין in pair by pair. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording implies a limit. He may wear one pair at a time, but not two or more pairs at once. The גמרא will now ask whose opinion this limit follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that follows the משנה
One pair: one set of head and hand תפילין
More (Aramaic)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
One pair, yes;
more — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier ruling in the משנה, that the תפילין are brought in pair by pair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה implies that only one pair of תפילין may be worn at a time.
steps.triggerLanguage: זוּג אֶחָד אִין טְפֵי לָא

steps.title: Does this unattributed משנה go against רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this unattributed משנה might not follow רבי מאיר, even though such a משנה usually does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that we learned an unattributed משנה that does not follow רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible problem. A limit of one pair seems to go against רבי מאיר, yet an unattributed משנה usually follows him. This question sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that an unattributed משנה (סתם משנה) usually reflects רבי מאיר's view. As the גמרא will go on to explain, רבי מאיר holds elsewhere that one may wear as much as he can. If so, the one-pair limit seems to contradict him, and the גמרא wants to resolve this.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say: introduces a suggestion the גמרא may later reject
An unattributed ruling (סתם משנה)
Not in accordance with רבי מאיר

steps.confusionAlert: The word לימא does not state a conclusion. It only floats a suggestion, and the גמרא often goes on to reject it and show that the משנה can fit everyone.

phrases.english: Shall we say we learned an unattributed teaching
that is not in accordance with Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the inference of step 6 and asks whose view it reflects.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the one-pair limit means this unattributed משנה goes against רבי מאיר.
steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תְּנַן סְתָמָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר

steps.title: רבי מאיר lets a person wear many garments to save them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its suggestion. In the fire case, רבי מאיר allows wearing as many garments as possible, so the one-pair limit on תפילין does not seem to fit his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: If our משנה followed רבי מאיר, there would be a problem. He says a person may put on all the clothes he can and wrap himself in all he can. We learned this in a משנה about a fire on שבת: one may take all his utensils out to the safe courtyard, and put on and wrap himself in everything he can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it suspects our משנה is not רבי מאיר's. It points to a fire case where רבי מאיר allows wearing many items at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה limits the finder to one pair of תפילין at a time. רבי מאיר lets a person wear unlimited garments to save them from a fire. So it seems רבי מאיר would also allow many pairs of תפילין, and our limit must come from someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Puts on, wears (a garment)
Wraps oneself (in a cloak or shawl)
His household utensils

phrases.english: For if it is like Rabbi Meir, didn't he say:
one puts on all that he is able to wear,
and wraps himself in all that he is able to wrap.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: וּלְשָׁם מוֹצִיא כׇּל כְּלֵי תַשְׁמִישׁוֹ,
phrases.english: As we learned: And to there one takes out all his utensils,
phrases.notes: "There" means the courtyard next to the fire, in the משנה in שבת about saving things from a fire.

phrases.english: and puts on all that he is able to wear,
and wraps himself in all that he is able to wrap.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind step 7's suggestion that the unattributed משנה is not רבי מאיר's.
steps.raayaObject: That the one-pair limit on תפילין does not match רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about saving things from a fire on שבת, where a person may wear as many garments as he can.

steps.title: How do we know the fire ruling is רבי מאיר's?
steps.stepSummary: The fire משנה has no name on it. The גמרא asks how we know it is רבי מאיר's.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that unattributed משנה: how do we know it is רבי מאיר's?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to check that the fire ruling really belongs to רבי מאיר. It is setting up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fire משנה is quoted without a name. The argument only works if that ruling truly is רבי מאיר's, so the גמרא must confirm who said it.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed ruling, quoted with no author named
From where do we know?

phrases.english: And that unattributed ruling,
from where do we know that it is Rabbi Meir's?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַהִיא סְתָמָא, מִמַּאי דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks who authored the source used in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the unattributed fire ruling follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: The continuation of the fire teaching names רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The teaching continues: a person may put on clothes, carry them out, and take them off, again and again all day long. These are named as the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The teaching goes on to say about that case: he puts on, takes out, and takes off. Then he puts on, takes out, and takes off again, even all day long. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The lines right after the fire ruling are labeled as רבי מאיר's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next part of the same teaching is credited to רבי מאיר by name, so the unattributed line before it is his too. This confirms that רבי מאיר holds a very lenient view about wearing items to save them.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it teaches about it, in the continuation of the same teaching
Takes off (a garment)

phrases.english: Since it teaches about it:
he puts on, takes out, and takes off,
and puts on, takes out, and takes off again,
even the entire day,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקָתָנֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The continuation of that teaching is credited to רבי מאיר by name, so the whole teaching follows him.

steps.title: רבא: in both cases the rule follows normal weekday wearing
steps.stepSummary: רבא says our משנה can follow רבי מאיר. In both cases the חכמים allowed carrying an item only in its normal way of wearing, just as on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say it follows רבי מאיר. There, wearing clothes in the usual way was treated by the חכמים like a weekday. Here too, wearing תפילין in the usual way was treated by the חכמים like a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the view that our משנה follows רבי מאיר. He gives one principle that covers both the clothing case and the תפילין case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission was never "wear as much as you can." It was "wear the item the way you normally wear it on a weekday." Because the same principle applies to both cases, there is no contradiction. The next step shows why the results still differ.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
The normal way it is worn
Like a weekday
The חכמים treated it as

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is saying רבי מאיר is strict here. רבא uses the very same lenient principle for both cases. The two cases differ only because normal weekday wearing is different for clothes than for תפילין.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: Rava said: You can even say it is Rabbi Meir,
there, wearing in its normal way —
the Sages treated it like a weekday,
and here, wearing in its normal way —
the Sages treated it like a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion from steps 7 to 10 that our משנה cannot be רבי מאיר's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shared principle (סברא) that explains both cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר allows wearing as many items as possible, so the one-pair limit cannot be his.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר allows wearing items only in their normal weekday manner, which fits both cases.

steps.title: Many garments are normal, but only one pair of תפילין
steps.stepSummary: On a weekday a person may wear as many clothes as he likes, so he may do the same to save them. On a weekday a person wears only one pair of תפילין, so to save them he may also wear only one pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since on a weekday a person may wear as much as he wants, the חכמים also allowed it for saving things. Here, even on a weekday one pair is allowed and more is not. So for saving them too, one pair is allowed and more is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies his principle to each case. This explains why the two cases end up with different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weekday norm sets the limit for the rescue permission. Clothes have no weekday limit, so they have no rescue limit. תפילין are limited to one pair even on a weekday, so the rescue permission is limited to one pair too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rescue, saving items
One pair (of תפילין)
More
They permitted

steps.whatToRemember: The rescue permission follows how an item is normally worn on a weekday. Clothes: as many as you like. תפילין: one pair. So our משנה fits רבי מאיר after all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a leniency based on "normal wearing" carries the natural limits of that wearing. It also keeps the unattributed משנה in line with רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: There, where on a weekday he wears as much as he wants,

phrases.aramaic: לְעִנְיַן הַצָּלָה נָמֵי שָׁרוּ לֵיה רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: for rescue also the Sages permitted it to him.
Here, where even on a weekday
one pair — yes, more — no,
for rescue also
one pair — yes, more — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם דִּבְחוֹל כַּמָּה דְּבָעֵי לָבֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how רבא's principle from step 11 leads to different results in the two cases.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה can follow רבי מאיר. A person saving תפילין may wear only one pair at a time, because that is the normal weekday way of wearing them.

steps.title: What is רבן גמליאל's reasoning for two pairs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן גמליאל's view in the משנה, that one brings in תפילין two pairs at a time, and asks what his reasoning is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: two by two. What does he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבן גמליאל's opinion from the משנה and asks what idea stands behind it. This sets up a two-sided challenge in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא explained the first opinion, which allows one pair at a time. Now it looks at רבן גמליאל, who allows two pairs. It wants to know which basic view about תפילין on שבת could lead to exactly two pairs.

keyTerms.meaning: Two by two, meaning two pairs at a time
What does he hold? A request for the reasoning behind a view

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says: two by two.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה about rescuing תפילין found in a field on שבת.

phrases.english: What does he hold?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first opinion in the משנה was explained, the גמרא moves on to רבן גמליאל's opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What basic view about תפילין on שבת leads רבן גמליאל to allow exactly two pairs?

steps.title: If שבת is a time for תפילין, only one pair should be allowed
steps.stepSummary: The first possibility: if רבן גמליאל holds that שבת is a time for תפילין, then one pair should be allowed and no more.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he holds that שבת is a time for תפילין, then one pair, yes; more, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible reasoning and shows that it does not fit רבן גמליאל's ruling of two pairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תפילין may properly be worn on שבת, then wearing them is just like a weekday, when a person wears one pair. A second pair would not be a real, proper wearing, so it would count as carrying. That leads to one pair, not two.

keyTerms.meaning: A time when one may or should wear תפילין
One pair (one head תפילין and one arm תפילין)
More

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר שַׁבָּת זְמַן תְּפִילִּין הוּא,
phrases.english: If he holds that Shabbat is a time for tefillin,
then one pair, yes; more, no.
phrases.notes: Only one pair counts as proper wearing, as on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קָסָבַר שַׁבָּת זְמַן תְּפִילִּין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first side of the two-sided challenge that grows out of the question in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that רבן גמליאל holds שבת is a time for תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שבת is a time for תפילין, a person wears them as on a weekday, which means one pair only. That contradicts רבן גמליאל's two pairs.

steps.title: If שבת is not a time for תפילין, even more than two should be allowed
steps.stepSummary: The second possibility: if שבת is not a time for תפילין, and the חכמים allowed wearing them only to save them, then even more than two pairs should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he holds that שבת is not a time for תפילין, and the חכמים allowed him to wear them only to save them, by way of wearing, then even more should be allowed too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other possible reasoning and shows that it also does not fit, because it would allow more than two pairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wearing תפילין on שבת is only a way to rescue them, it is like the fire case, where a person may wear as many garments as he can. By that logic there should be no limit at two pairs. So neither side seems to explain רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Rescue, saving an item from being lost or damaged
The normal way of wearing something
The חכמים permitted it to him

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי קָסָבַר שַׁבָּת לָאו זְמַן תְּפִילִּין הוּא,
phrases.english: And if he holds that Shabbat is not a time for tefillin,
and it is because of rescue, by way of wearing,
that the Sages permitted it to him,
then even more should also be allowed!
phrases.notes: Like the fire case, where one may wear as many garments as possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי קָסָבַר שַׁבָּת לָאו זְמַן תְּפִילִּין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This completes the two-sided challenge: the first side led to too few pairs, and this side leads to too many.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that רבן גמליאל holds שבת is not a time for תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If wearing is only for rescue, there is no reason to stop at two pairs. Any number that can be worn should be allowed.

steps.title: Not a time for תפילין, but they must be worn in their proper place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבן גמליאל holds שבת is not a time for תפילין, but the rescue was allowed only by wearing them in the place where תפילין are worn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he holds that שבת is not a time for תפילין. But when the חכמים allowed rescue, it was by way of wearing, in the place of תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks the second view and adds a limit: the תפילין must be worn in their proper place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rescue is allowed only by wearing, and wearing תפילין means putting them where תפילין go. Putting them anywhere else on the body is carrying, not wearing. This limit explains why there is no unlimited number of pairs.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact; it keeps one side of the choice and adds an explanation
In the place where תפילין are worn (head and arm)

steps.confusionAlert: Wearing תפילין here is not the מצוה of תפילין, since שבת is not a time for תפילין. It is only a permitted way to carry them in, by wearing them, so they are rescued.

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר שַׁבָּת לָאו זְמַן תְּפִילִּין הוּא,
phrases.english: Actually, he holds that Shabbat is not a time for tefillin,
and when the Sages permitted it for the purpose of rescue,
it was by way of wearing, in the place of tefillin.
phrases.notes: Anywhere else on the body would count as carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר שַׁבָּת לָאו זְמַן תְּפִילִּין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge of step 15 by limiting how the rescue may be done.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a limiting condition (proper place) to the rescue permission
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the wearing is only for rescue, any number of pairs should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rescue is allowed only by wearing in the place of תפילין, which limits how many can be worn.

steps.title: Then only one pair should fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the תפילין must be in their proper place, only one pair fits there, so more should not be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then one pair, yes; more, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, saying it now leads to only one pair, not two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There seems to be room for only one תפילין on the head. A second pair would have to go somewhere else, which would be carrying. So the answer seems to support the first opinion, not רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; it introduces a challenge built on the last answer

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי זוּג אֶחָד נָמֵי — אֵין,
phrases.english: If so, then one pair, yes,
but more, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי זוּג אֶחָד נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the answer of step 16 by using its own condition against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that rescue must be in the place of תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The place of תפילין seems to hold only one pair, so the second pair would be out of place and forbidden.

steps.title: The head has room for two תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק answers that the head has enough room to place two תפילין, so two pairs can be properly worn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: There is room on the head to place two תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק solves the problem by pointing out that two תפילין fit in the proper place on the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both head תפילין can sit in the right place, wearing two head תפילין counts as real wearing and not as carrying. This answers the challenge for the head only. The next step asks whether the arm also has room for two.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room on the head
To place (put on)

steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל holds שבת is not a time for תפילין. They may be rescued only by wearing them in their proper place. The head has room for two תפילין. The next step asks whether the arm also has room, and step 22 answers that it does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the exact number in רבן גמליאל's ruling. The number of pairs depends on how many can be worn in the proper place.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak said:
There is room on the head
to place two tefillin on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: מָקוֹם יֵשׁ בָּרֹאשׁ לְהַנִּיחַ בּוֹ שְׁתֵּי תְפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge of step 17 and completes the explanation of רבן גמליאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification about how much space there is on the head
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one pair fits in the proper place, so only one pair should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two תפילין fit on the head, so two pairs can be properly worn, and רבן גמליאל's ruling stands.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The head has room for two תפילין, so two head תפילין can be worn properly. The arm still needs to be addressed (steps 19–22).

steps.title: The head has room, but what about the arm?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that two של ראש fit on the head, but asks how two של יד can fit on the arm.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works well for the head תפילין. But for the arm תפילין, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that the head has room for two תפילין, but now asks how the arm can hold two pairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק only showed that the head has space for two. But a pair of תפילין is one של ראש and one של יד. So if the arm has no room for a second של יד, the rescue still fails for the second pair.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (this part makes sense)
Of the head (the תפילין של ראש)
Of the arm (the תפילין של יד)
What is there to say? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: It works out well for the head [תפילין];
but for the arm [תפילין], what is there to say?
phrases.notes: The previous answer covered only the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא דְּרֹאשׁ, דְּיָד מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of Step 18 for the head but shows it does not cover the arm.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of רב שמואל בר רב יצחק (Step 18), which only addressed the head.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full pair needs both a head and an arm תפילין in their proper places. Room on the head alone does not let two full pairs be worn properly.

steps.title: Answer from רב הונא: tefillin may be moved to the arm
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from רב הונא, who said a person carrying a load on his head may move his head תפילין onto his arm. This suggests the arm has room for more than one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רב הונא said. Sometimes a person comes from the field with his bundle on his head. He removes the תפילין from his head and ties them on his arm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove the arm can hold extra תפילין by quoting רב הונא, who allowed moving the head תפילין onto the arm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הונא's case, the person already wears an arm תפילין. If he may also tie the head תפילין onto his arm, the arm seems to have room for two. That would answer the question of Step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
His bundle or load
And he removes them
And ties them on his arm

phrases.english: It is in accordance with Rav Huna,
as Rav Huna said:
Sometimes a person comes from the field
with his bundle on his head,
and he removes them [the תפילין] from his head
and ties them on his arm.
phrases.notes: The arm now holds both the arm and head תפילין.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19 by bringing a source that suggests the arm can hold two תפילין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Support from an earlier ruling (רב הונא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The arm seemed to have room for only one תפילין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The proposal: since רב הונא allows tying a second תפילין on the arm, the arm has room for two. Step 21 rejects this proof.

steps.title: רב הונא was only preventing disrespect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רב הונא only allowed moving the תפילין to avoid disrespecting them, not because the arm is a proper place for two.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say that רב הונא said this so that he would not treat them in a disrespectful way. But did he say the place is fit for them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from רב הונא. Moving the head תפילין to the arm was only an emergency step to protect them from a load on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's ruling is about avoiding בזיון (disrespect), not about a proper way to wear תפילין. Tying them on the arm protects them, but that does not make the arm a fit place for them. We need a fit place, because the rescue on שבת works only by wearing the תפילין properly (Step 16).

keyTerms.meaning: Say (you could say that…)
In a disrespectful way
Fit or proper (a valid place to wear them)
Did he say? (a rhetorical question meaning he did not)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב הונא is wrong. The גמרא only says his ruling does not prove what we need. Protecting תפילין from disrespect is not the same as wearing them properly.

phrases.english: Say that Rav Huna said [this]
so that he will not treat them in a degrading manner.
Did he say [the place is] fit?
phrases.notes: He's asking it as a challenge, and the answer is no, he did not say that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from רב הונא brought in Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the use of רב הונא as proof, not רב הונא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב הונא's ruling is about avoiding disrespect, not about the arm being a proper (ראוי) place for two תפילין, which the שבת rescue requires.

steps.title: The arm, like the head, has room for two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes by applying רב שמואל בר רב יצחק's idea to the arm. Just as the head has room for two תפילין, so does the arm.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: there is room on the head to place two תפילין. Here too, there is room on the arm to place two תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the proof from רב הונא, the גמרא goes back to רב שמואל בר רב יצחק's principle and applies it to the arm too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proper place for the arm תפילין is big enough for two, just like the proper place on the head. So a person can properly wear two full pairs at once. This explains why רבן גמליאל allowed two pairs on שבת, but not more.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the earlier answer)
There is room (a place)
Here too (the same applies)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן גמליאל, שבת is not a time for תפילין. They may be rescued only by wearing them properly. The proper places on both the head and the arm have room for two, so exactly two pairs may be worn, and no more.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the explanation of why רבן גמליאל allows exactly two pairs. It answers both sides of the earlier challenge: why more than one pair, and why not more than two.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּדְאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, it is like what Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak said:
There is room on the head
that is fit to place two tefillin on it.
Here too, there is room on the arm
that is fit to place two tefillin on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּדְאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 21 rejects רב הונא, this gives the final answer to Step 19 by applying רב שמואל בר רב יצחק's principle to the arm.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the head and the arm have a proper place big enough for two תפילין, so two pairs may be worn properly. That is why רבן גמליאל allows saving exactly two pairs.

steps.title: The exact places for תפילין on the arm and head
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of מנשה teaches that 'on your arm' means the biceps, and 'between your eyes' means the crown of the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of מנשה taught: 'On your arm' means the biceps muscle. 'Between your eyes' means the crown of the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that explains exactly where on the body the פסוק wants תפילין to be placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'between your eyes', but this ברייתא teaches that it does not mean literally on the forehead between the eyes. It means higher up, on the top of the head. Both places it names, the biceps and the crown, are wide areas, which fits the idea from step 22 that there is room for two תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the study hall of מנשה
'On your arm', from the פסוק about תפילין
The biceps, the raised muscle of the upper arm
'Between your eyes', from the פסוק
The crown, the top of the head

steps.confusionAlert: 'Between your eyes' does NOT mean on the forehead between the eyebrows. The ברייתא teaches it means the top of the head.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for where תפילין are actually placed in practice: the של יד on the biceps and the של ראש above the hairline.

phrases.english: The school of Menashe taught:
"On your arm" — this is the biceps muscle,
"between your eyes" — this is the crown of the head.
phrases.notes: This is from the פסוק in דברים ו:ח.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא דְבֵי מְנַשֶּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After concluding that the arm and head each have room for two תפילין, the גמרא defines exactly where those places are.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The arm תפילין go on the biceps, and the head תפילין go on the crown of the head.

steps.title: Where exactly on the crown of the head?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the precise spot on the top of the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where exactly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: where on the top of the head do the תפילין go? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'crown of the head' is a large area. The גמרא wants a more exact location.

keyTerms.meaning: Where?

phrases.english: Where?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for more detail about the 'crown of the head' mentioned in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The precise spot on the crown of the head where the head תפילין are placed.

steps.title: The soft spot of a baby's head
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי answers: the place where a baby's skull is soft.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי say: It is the spot where a baby's head is soft.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The head תפילין go on the spot that is soft on a newborn's head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Newborns have a soft spot on top of the skull that hardens later. That spot marks where the head תפילין belong. This gives a clear physical sign anyone can identify.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ינאי say
His brain, here meaning the skull area
Soft, yielding

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical marker used to place the head תפילין correctly.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
The place where a baby's skull is soft.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The head תפילין are placed where a baby's skull is soft.

steps.title: Is the dispute in the משנה about room for two pairs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the תנא קמא disagrees with רב שמואל בר רב יצחק, while רבן גמליאל agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about the idea of רב שמואל בר רב יצחק? The תנא קמא does not accept his idea, and רבן גמליאל does accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about rescuing תפילין on שבת and suggests a reason for the argument there. This is only a suggestion, and the גמרא will test it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the תנא קמא says to bring the תפילין in one pair at a time, while רבן גמליאל says two pairs at a time. The suggestion is that the תנא קמא thinks there is no room for two pairs, so the second pair is just a burden. רבן גמליאל agrees there is room for two, so wearing two pairs is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? A suggestion the גמרא is testing
They disagree
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
He does not hold of
He holds of

steps.confusionAlert: 'לֵימָא' is only a suggestion. Usually the גמרא rejects it right away, as it does here.

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא בִּדְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק קָמִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: Shall we say they disagree about the view of Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak,
that the first tanna does not hold
the view of Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak,
and Rabban Gamliel does hold
the view of Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּדְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having established that there is room for two תפילין, the גמרא asks whether this explains the dispute in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's dispute (one pair vs. two pairs) depends on accepting רב שמואל בר רב יצחק's view that there is room for two.

steps.title: Everyone agrees there is room; the dispute is whether שבת is a time for תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone accepts רב שמואל בר רב יצחק. The argument is whether שבת is a time for תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone accepts the view of רב שמואל בר רב יצחק. Here they argue about whether שבת is a time for תפילין. The תנא קמא holds that שבת is a time for תפילין. רבן גמליאל holds that שבת is not a time for תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the suggestion is wrong and gives a different reason for the argument in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שבת IS a time for תפילין, then wearing a second pair adds to the מצוה, which is forbidden (בל תוסיף). So the second pair counts as a burden, and only one pair at a time may be brought in. If שבת is NOT a time for תפילין, there is no מצוה at all, so wearing two pairs adds nothing. They are treated like clothing, and two pairs may be brought in together, since the proper places have room for two.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
A time when one is obligated to wear תפילין
Holds, is of the opinion
Not

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree there is room for two pairs. The real question is whether שבת is a time for תפילין. If it is (תנא קמא), a second pair would add to the מצוה, so only one pair at a time. If it is not (רבן גמליאל), two pairs are allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards that the side holding 'שבת is a time for תפילין' is the stricter one. But that is exactly the point: if there is a מצוה, a second pair adds to it and becomes a forbidden burden.
steps.whyThisMatters: The halacha follows the view that שבת is not a time for תפילין, which is why we do not wear תפילין on שבת.

phrases.english: No, everyone holds
the view of Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak,
and here they disagree about whether Shabbat is a time for tefillin.
For the first tanna holds:
Shabbat is a time for tefillin.
phrases.notes: So a second pair would add to the מצוה and count as a burden.

phrases.english: And Rabban Gamliel holds:
Shabbat is not a time for tefillin.
phrases.notes: So there is no מצוה to add to, and two pairs may be worn like clothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 26 and moves the dispute to a different issue.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the תנא קמא disagrees with רב שמואל בר רב יצחק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed the dispute was about physical room. In fact both agree there is room, and the dispute is about whether שבת is a time for תפילין, which decides whether a second pair adds to the מצוה.

steps.title: A different explanation: the argument is about intent for מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way to explain the argument. Both sides agree that שבת is a time for תפילין. Their disagreement is whether מצוות צריכות כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say this instead: everyone agrees that שבת is a time for תפילין. Here they argue about whether מצוות require intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, alternative explanation of why the תנא קמא and רבן גמליאל disagree. This step only names the new topic of the argument; the next step will explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27, the argument depended on whether שבת is a time for תפילין. Now that question is taken off the table, because here everyone says yes. The argument moves to a completely different issue: does a person need כוונה (intent) for a מצוה to count?

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say': introduces an alternative explanation
Everyone agrees
A time when the מצוה of תפילין applies
מצוות require intent: the person must intend to do the מצוה
They disagree

steps.confusionAlert: This does NOT cancel step 27. 'ואיבעית אימא' means both explanations stand side by side as possible ways to understand the argument. The גמרא is offering a second option, not rejecting the first.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
phrases.notes: Here comes a second way to explain it.

phrases.english: that everyone agrees
Shabbat is a time for tefillin,
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of the first explanation, where this point was the argument.

phrases.english: and here, about whether מצוות require intent,

steps.title: Each side's view on intent
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that a person needs כוונה to fulfill a מצוה. רבן גמליאל holds that no כוונה is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds that to fulfill a מצוה you need intent. רבן גמליאל holds that you do not need intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out each side of the new explanation. This is how the different rulings about bringing in the found תפילין come about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, wearing תפילין without כוונה is not a מצוה, so it is just carrying a burden. He must wear them with כוונה, but then a second pair would be adding to the מצוה (בל תוסיף), so only one pair is allowed. According to רבן גמליאל, the first pair counts automatically even without כוונה. The second pair is only a problem of adding to the מצוה if he specifically intends it as an extra מצוה, so two pairs are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The second explanation: everyone agrees שבת is a time for תפילין. The argument is about כוונה. The תנא קמא says one needs כוונה, so only one pair is allowed. רבן גמליאל says one does not need כוונה, so two pairs are allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links a specific case of rescuing תפילין to one of the most famous general questions in the תורה: whether a מצוה counts without intent.

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
To fulfill a מצוה, one needs intent.
phrases.notes: So wearing without intent is not a מצוה. With intent, a second pair would be adding to the מצוה.

phrases.english: And Rabban Gamliel holds:
One does not need intent.
phrases.notes: So one pair counts automatically, and a second pair is not considered adding unless he specifically intends it.
